To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aflatoxins, which are known to cause liver cancer, are present in food in Egypt and that the levels in food are higher in the north of the country than in the south.
we have detected aflatoxin– albumin (AF– albs) adducts in 24/ 24 HCC negative individuals and 7/ 22 HCC positive cases in Egypt.
aflatoxins are a major food-borne carcinogen in developing countries and the level of aflotoxin–albumin biomarker in serum was measured for the first time in Egypt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of risk factors for HCC, a cancer with a high mortality rate.
the development of an analytical method for the determination of the biomarker of aflatoxin B1–albumin adduction in human serum samples.
the potential health consequences associated with exposure to aflatoxin, and the role of aflatoxin in the development of HCC.

the data are limited and do not represent a comparison of aflatoxin exposures in controls and patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
aflatoxin exposure has not been demonstrated to be associated with HCC in Egypt.
the presence of AF–alb adducts in serum samples from Egypt indicates that aflatoxins are present in the diet and that there may be a potential health risk to the local population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aflatoxin exposure is likely to occur in Egypt and may contribute to the high rates of HCC in this population.
aflatoxins are present in Egyptian food and are a potential risk for HCC.
aflatoxins are present in Egyptian cereals, and the presence of the AF-alb adducts in the sera of the Egyptian population is indicative of aflatoxin intake.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aflatoxin–serum albumin adduct is a useful biomarker for assessing aflatoxin exposure and the risk of liver cancer in Egypt.
